analysis: The only change in StandaloneServer.swift is in the periodic KV sweep task (head lines ~562-568). The task now captures [weak self, kvBudget] and calls `await self?.retryShapeWarmups()` before `kvBudget.proactiveReclaimSweep()`. The supplied units are unchanged BASE text for lines 1220-2271 (reslice, eviction, model load). The changed lines are not visible in these units, so I cannot cite or inspect the new call or retryShapeWarmups itself. In the visible context I examined the load, eviction and reslice paths. They show no security-relevant changes: the slot reservation, evictingModels and isLoadingAny guards, the GLM and MiMo retirement ordering, and the SSD cache weight-hash bracket (T-041) are all unchanged. The weak self capture avoids a retain cycle and does not touch trust boundaries. The new warmup retry runs on a periodic timer, and I could not inspect its implementation. Questions for deeper review: (1) Does retryShapeWarmups bypass the isLoadingAny/load-gate serialization or memory admission, or run MLX work concurrently with a model load? (2) Does it hold GPU or memory budget without a pending-load lease? (3) Could it touch prefix-cache state (T-041) or leave stale state across evictions? The patch comment says a session skips the sweep and a flush could cancel it, which suggests a scheduling concern rather than a security issue. No concrete regression is identified in the supplied evidence. The warmup implementation lies outside the supplied units.
